tier_reason: Project's own wiki page benchmarks Pipy vs nginx (1 worker, distro package nginx/1.18.0) and hashicorp http-echo with full wrk/ab/fortio command lines and raw outputs; wrk Ubuntu21-arm64 rows show 82759.60 (nginx) vs 218539.23 (pipy) req/s. No CPU model, compiler or build flags stated (only a 2 vCPU/4GB ARM64 VM), so first-party with partial methodology = C.

corrections.workload: HTTP GET 'hello world' via wrk -c100 -t1 -d20 --latency (100 connections, 1 wrk thread, 20s), client and server on the same 2 vCPU/4GB ARM64 VM over 127.0.0.1; Ubuntu 21 Server and FreeBSD 13; Pipy script tutorial/02-echo/hello.js; also ab (short-lived connections) and fortio (fixed 10k QPS latency)
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark (project's own wiki), partial methodology: no compiler/build flags and no CPU model (only '2 vcpus', '2C4G', ARM64), so capped at tier C although command lines and raw tool outputs are published. The 2.6x headline is the most favorable row: on FreeBSD13 wrk the gap is 281176 vs 204544 req/s (~1.37x, derived from page data); with ab short-lived connections Pipy roughly ties nginx (Ubuntu 59698 vs 60824, FreeBSD 95074 vs 93680); fortio P50 latency on Ubuntu is worse for Pipy (1.851ms vs 1.449ms). Raw wrk output shows nginx returned larger responses (393.12MB for 1.66M requests vs Pipy 308.60MB for 4.37M), i.e. more header bytes per reply. nginx was a distro package with 1 worker; Pipy built from source. Old test (nginx 1.18.0/1.20.2, Ubuntu 21), not re-run on current Pipy. LICENSE file: Pipy itself MIT; bundled deps (Boost Asio, OpenSSL 1.1.1o, zlib, SQLite, etc.) carry their own licenses (GitHub reports NOASSERTION).

notes: Numbers verified verbatim in summary table (cases 4 and 6) and raw wrk appendices. Metadata checked via gh: 832 stars, not fork/archived, last commit 2026-06-12 (active), LICENSE text is MIT for Pipy. Only caveats/workload refined to reflect the less favorable rows.
